title: Koba akondro (Malagasy steamed peanut and banana cakes)

ingredients.name: banana leaves, or squares of baking parchment and foil

steps: Mix the ground peanuts, mashed bananas, honey, cornmeal and salt into a thick, sticky batter.
If using banana leaves, hold them briefly over a flame or dip in hot water so they turn pliable; cut them into squares about 25 cm across.
Spoon about 3 tablespoons of batter into the middle of each square and fold the leaf into a tight, sealed parcel, tying with kitchen string if needed.
Set up a steamer or a pot with a rack and about 3 cm of simmering water.
Steam the parcels for 45 to 60 minutes, topping up with boiling water as needed, until the batter is firm.
Let the parcels cool for 10 minutes, then unwrap and slice or serve whole.
Eat warm or at room temperature as a snack or dessert.

title: Lasary (Malagasy vegetable salad in vinaigrette)

ingredients.name: green beans, trimmed and cut into short lengths

steps: Boil the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes, adding the carrots for the last 2 minutes, then drain and cool under cold water.
Salt the shredded cabbage lightly and leave it for 10 minutes, then squeeze out any liquid.
Whisk the oil, vinegar or lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Combine the beans, carrots, cabbage and onion in a large bowl.
Pour over the dressing, add the chilli if using, and toss well.
Let the salad rest for 15 to 20 minutes so the vegetables absorb the dressing.
Serve alongside rice and grilled meats, or tuck into a baguette.

title: Misao (Malagasy Chinese-style stir-fried noodles)

ingredients.name: chicken breast or pork, thinly sliced

steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet until just tender, drain and rinse with cold water to stop them sticking.
Heat the oil in a wok or large pan over high heat and stir-fry the meat for 4 to 5 minutes until cooked through; remove and set aside.
Add the onion, garlic and carrots to the pan and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the cabbage and cook for 2 minutes more, until it begins to wilt but still has bite.
If using eggs, push the vegetables aside, scramble the eggs in the gap, then mix them through.
Return the meat to the pan, add the noodles and soy sauce, and toss everything together over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve straight from the pan.

title: Mofo gasy (Malagasy rice flour breakfast cakes)

ingredients.name: warm water or half water and half coconut milk

steps: Whisk the rice flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together in a bowl.
Pour in the warm water or coconut milk and the vanilla, and whisk to a smooth batter about as thick as pancake batter.
Rest the batter for 20 minutes so the rice flour hydrates.
Heat a small-welled pan, such as a poffertjes, aebleskiver or muffin-style pan, over medium-low heat and brush each well with oil.
Fill each well about three quarters full with batter.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes until the edges set and the undersides are golden, then flip and cook the other side for 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve warm for breakfast with coffee or sweet tea; they are best eaten fresh.

title: Ravitoto (Malagasy pounded cassava leaves with pork)

ingredients.name: cassava leaves, finely ground (frozen, or substitute collard greens finely chopped)
pork belly or fatty pork shoulder, cut into cubes

steps: Cook the cassava leaves, if fresh or frozen, in a pot of boiling water for 15 minutes, then drain well; collard greens need only about 10 minutes.
Pound or process the leaves with a little of the garlic until they form a coarse, dense paste.
In a heavy pot, fry the pork cubes in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until the fat renders and the meat is lightly browned.
Add the onion and remaining garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the leaf paste, add the water and a little salt, and mix well.
Cover and simmer very gently for 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally and adding a splash of water if it sticks, until the pork is meltingly tender and the greens are dark and thick.
Taste, adjust the salt and serve with plenty of white rice.

title: Romazava (Malagasy beef and greens broth)

ingredients.name: beef chuck or stewing beef, cut into chunks
mixed leafy greens such as spinach, watercress and mustard greens (traditionally brèdes mafana, anamalaho)

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef chunks in two batches for about 8 minutes each, then set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and ginger and stir for a minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they begin to break down.
Return the beef to the pot, add the water and a good pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for about 1 hour, until the meat is tender.
Wash the greens, tear or chop them roughly and stir them into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes, until the greens are wilted but still bright, and adjust the seasoning.
Serve the brothy stew in bowls with plenty of white rice, as is done for most Malagasy meals.
